canonical_statement: The integration of new information can enrich or modify existing knowledge structures.

attributions.surface_quote: the apperceiving mass ('table') is enriched

canonical_statement: Existing conceptual frameworks, often termed 'a priori', are generally more influential in processing new information than the new information itself.

attributions.surface_quote: the a priori factor is almost always the more active

canonical_statement: Consciousness tends to assimilate new experiences by fitting them into pre-existing conceptual frameworks, modifying the frameworks minimally.

attributions.surface_quote: Every new experience must be disposed of under some old head.

canonical_statement: The capacity to form new conceptual frameworks is a characteristic of genius.

attributions.surface_quote: Genius, in truth, means little more than the faculty of perceiving in an unhabitual way.

canonical_statement: Established conceptual frameworks can prevent the assimilation of novel or contradictory experiences.

attributions.surface_quote: Objects which violate our established habits of 'apperception' are simply not taken account of at all.

canonical_statement: The mind exhibits a tension between the desire to maintain existing ideas and the drive to create new ones.

attributions.surface_quote: There is an everlasting struggle in every mind between the tendency to keep unchanged, and the tendency to renovate, its ideas.

canonical_statement: Consciousness categorizes novel experiences by relating them to pre-existing conceptual frameworks.

attributions.surface_quote: assimilate the new to the old, to meet each threatening violator or burster of our well-known series of concepts

canonical_statement: The drive to understand is contingent upon the existence of prior conceptual frameworks.

attributions.surface_quote: Only what we partly know already inspires us with a desire to know more.

canonical_statement: Novelty that is too far removed from existing conceptual frameworks elicits no cognitive response.

attributions.surface_quote: things so far beyond us that we have no concepts to refer them to or standards by which to measure them

canonical_statement: Perception is a form of reasoning or inference.

attributions.surface_quote: perception should be called a sort of reasoning operation

canonical_statement: The inferential processes underlying perception can occur unconsciously.

attributions.surface_quote: more or less unconsciously and automatically performed

canonical_statement: The assumption of unconscious inferential processes in perception leads to an infinite regress.

attributions.surface_quote: should, if all perception were inference, require a still earlier syllogism

canonical_statement: Perception and reasoning are distinct but co-ordinate processes stemming from a deeper psychological principle of association and a physiological law of habit.

attributions.surface_quote: perception and reasoning are co-ordinate varieties of that deeper sort of process

canonical_statement: The assertion that perception is unconscious reasoning is either a metaphor or a confusion.

attributions.surface_quote: To call perception unconscious reasoning is thus either a useless metaphor

canonical_statement: The brain's habitual connections facilitate the association of ideas and sensations.

attributions.surface_quote: habit-worn paths in the brain makes such images entirely superfluous

canonical_statement: Perception, unlike explicit reasoning, likely does not involve traversing indirect associative pathways.

attributions.surface_quote: in perception they are in all probability closed

canonical_statement: Consciousness exhibits an inverse relationship between the intensity of knowledge/perception and the intensity of feeling/sensation.

attributions.surface_quote: Knowledge and Feeling,--Perception and Sensation, though always coexistent, are always in the inverse ratio of each other.

canonical_statement: States of consciousness are more vivid when they are more concentrated.

attributions.surface_quote: the more concentrated a state of consciousness is, the more vivid it is.

canonical_statement: Intense sensory experience is incompatible with highly diffused cerebral excitement.

attributions.surface_quote: The more diffused cerebral excitement of the perceptive state is probably incompatible with quite as strong an excitement of separate parts as the sensational state comports.

canonical_statement: Consciousness is a sensational form, indistinguishable from sensory experience even in the absence of external stimuli.

attributions.surface_quote: An hallucination is a strictly sensational form of consciousness

canonical_statement: The process of perception is continuous, with no fundamental distinction between veridical perception and illusion/hallucination.

attributions.surface_quote: Between normal perception and illusion we have seen that there is no break

canonical_statement: Hallucinations are extreme manifestations of the perception process, where internal cerebral activity disproportionately influences experience.

attributions.surface_quote: extremes of the perception process, in which the secondary cerebral reaction is out of all normal proportion

attributions.surface_quote: the identification of the two phenomena is impossible

canonical_statement: Subjective phenomena are experienced as distinct from objective reality, even by individuals with impaired cognitive function.

attributions.surface_quote: even though he be imbecile, the identification of the two phenomena is impossible

canonical_statement: The experience of a subjective phenomenon is differentiated from the experience of objective reality by the individual's relation to the phenomenon.

attributions.surface_quote: the patient feels himself in an entirely different relation to this subjective sensible appearance

canonical_statement: Hallucinations are perceived as objective reality, while pseudo-hallucinations are recognized as subjective phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: The latter is reality itself; the former, on the contrary, remains always a subjective phenomenon

canonical_statement: Consciousness can distinguish between internally generated perceptions and external reality.

attributions.surface_quote: he remained conscious... that he saw the animal, not with his bodily but with his mental eyes

canonical_statement: The mind can generate sensory experiences (visual, auditory, tactile) that are perceived as real.

attributions.surface_quote: pseudo-hallucination of touch... saw the animal... expressive-plastic ideas

attributions.surface_quote: recollected that the lion was the national emblem of England

attributions.surface_quote: accordingly he felt no terror... Had the lion been a complete hallucination... he would have felt great fear

attributions.surface_quote: entirely unlike the inner speech of the subject with himself

attributions.surface_quote: I tried to throw off the impression... the impression became a conviction

attributions.surface_quote: not conscious of having dreamed anything, but I was very firmly impressed

canonical_statement: Consciousness can experience direct intromission into alternate realities.

attributions.surface_quote: seemed like a direct intromission into some other world

canonical_statement: Perceptual experiences can include a sense of infinity and novel sensory qualities.

attributions.surface_quote: sense of infinity in nature, such superb stretches of light and color

canonical_statement: Altered states of consciousness can involve a temporary loss of orientation to physical location.

attributions.surface_quote: entirely lost, for when I began to come to, so to speak,--sitting in that other world

attributions.surface_quote: The following vivid account of a fit of hasheesh-delirium

attributions.surface_quote: countless other absurdities... creations of the brain.

canonical_statement: The mind can observe its own internal physiological processes.

attributions.surface_quote: see within myself, and watch the pumping of my heart.

canonical_statement: Subjective experience can shift rapidly between states of fear and intense interest.

attributions.surface_quote: strange fear... followed by a feeling of great interest.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can directly perceive or embody imagined realities.

attributions.surface_quote: Any place thought of or suggested appeared with all the distinctness of the reality.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can assume the identity and form of any object or being.

attributions.surface_quote: Any animal or thing that I thought of could be made the being which held my mind.

canonical_statement: The subjective experience of identity is not inherently tied to a physical body.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can experience reality from multiple, non-physical perspectives.

canonical_statement: Consciousness can experience the physical properties of imagined objects.

attributions.surface_quote: I was next transformed into a bombshell, felt my size, weight, and thickness...

canonical_statement: The range of possible conscious experiences is virtually limitless.

attributions.surface_quote: Into countless other objects was I transformed, many of them so absurd...

canonical_statement: Hallucination arises from internal excitation of perceptual centers, mirroring the process induced by external stimuli.

attributions.surface_quote: excitement from within of those centres which are active in normal perception

canonical_statement: The intensity of conscious experience correlates with the intensity of neural processes.

attributions.surface_quote: vividness of the sensational kind of consciousness is probably correlated with a discrete degree of intensity

canonical_statement: Perceptual centers are involved in both external perception and internal imagination.

attributions.surface_quote: centres aroused by incoming peripheral currents are probably identical with the centres used in mere imagination

attributions.surface_quote: if the leakage forward were to stop, the tension inside certain cells might reach the explosion-point

canonical_statement: External sensory input possesses a unique quality of energy capable of overcoming inherent cellular resistance, leading to intense disintegration associated with sensational experience.

attributions.surface_quote: Currents from the periphery are ... the only currents whose energy can vanquish the supra-ideational resistance

canonical_statement: The intensity of subjective experience (sensational activity) is directly proportional to the accumulation of internal tension within a neural center.

attributions.surface_quote: the pail promptly fills up ... upsets; in other words, sensational activity is aroused

canonical_statement: The normal flow of excitation between cortical cells results in ideational activity rather than intense sensational experience.

attributions.surface_quote: in the pail itself nothing but what stands for ideational activity is aroused

canonical_statement: The intensity of a conscious state is inversely proportional to its capacity to evoke further conscious states.

attributions.surface_quote: the substantive strength of a state of consciousness bears an inverse proportion to its suggestiveness

attributions.surface_quote: the moment the current is blocked anywhere... the process... must grow more intense

canonical_statement: Intense conscious states can manifest as sensory experiences or hallucinations.

attributions.surface_quote: might even be conceived to explode so as to produce a sensation in the mind instead of an idea

canonical_statement: Reduced associative processes correlate with heightened residual consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: associative processes are reduced and impeded... we find a concomitant increase in the intensity of whatever partial consciousness may survive

canonical_statement: Consciousness is a product of organized brain processes; disruption of these processes leads to loss of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: loss of consciousness in epilepsy is due to the most highly organized brain-processes being exhausted

canonical_statement: Lower-level mental processes can become dominant when higher-level inhibitory processes are absent.

attributions.surface_quote: less organized processes, ordinarily inhibited by the others, are then exalted

canonical_statement: The intensity of subjective experience is directly related to the intensity of the underlying neural process.

attributions.surface_quote: process of 'imagining' must be not merely relatively, but absolutely and in itself more intense

canonical_statement: Sensory input normally serves to ground subjective ideas in objective reality.

attributions.surface_quote: objects of our imagination are reduced to the status of subjective facts by the ever-present contrast of our sensations

canonical_statement: The absence of sensory input allows subjective ideas to be perceived as external realities.

attributions.surface_quote: Eliminate the sensations... and the 'images' are forthwith 'projected' into the outer world

canonical_statement: Consciousness intensity is amplified when normal associative pathways are disrupted, allowing internal activity to reach full sensational intensity.

attributions.surface_quote: normal paths of association... thrown out of gear... full sensational process explodes.

canonical_statement: External stimuli of insufficient intensity to normally produce sensation can trigger full sensational experiences when associative pathways are blocked.

attributions.surface_quote: slight peripheral irritation... will give rise to the dream of a violent sensation.

canonical_statement: Disruption of normal neural excitation pathways leads to amplified sensational experiences from minor stimuli.

attributions.surface_quote: normal forward irradiation... is checked... sets up a process of full sensational intensity.

attributions.surface_quote: Part of the thing in all cases comes from the sense-organ, the rest is furnished by the mind.

canonical_statement: Hallucinations and illusions can be understood as a physiological type of perception, initiated by peripheral stimuli.

attributions.surface_quote: all hallucinations must start in the periphery

canonical_statement: External objectivity in perception is contingent upon peripheral sensory excitation.

attributions.surface_quote: the dot is the outward point de repère which is needed to give objectivity to your suggestion

attributions.surface_quote: What the nature of the object shall be will depend wholly on the particular system of paths in which the process is kindled.

canonical_statement: Hallucinations can originate from internal mental processes rather than solely external sensory input.

attributions.surface_quote: centrally initiated hallucinations can exist

canonical_statement: The intensity of a perceptual experience can be generated by internal cortical activity.

attributions.surface_quote: degree in question might not be attained by inner causes exclusively

attributions.surface_quote: hallucinations which affect more than one sense is an argument for central initiation

canonical_statement: The temporal duration of the perceptive process is a measurable quantity.

attributions.surface_quote: The time which the perceptive process occupies has been inquired into.

canonical_statement: Hallucinations can coincide with external events.

attributions.surface_quote: many of them are reported as veridical, coinciding with real events

canonical_statement: The origin of hallucinations is not fully understood.

attributions.surface_quote: Sporadic cases of hallucination... are on any theory hard to understand

canonical_statement: The role of peripheral sense organs in hallucination is unclear.

attributions.surface_quote: The part played by the peripheral sense-organ in hallucination is just as obscure

attributions.surface_quote: a centrifugal current from the optical centres downwards into the peripheral organ of sight

attributions.surface_quote: faint and vague excitements of sense-organs are transformed into figured objects by the brain

attributions.surface_quote: excessive excitation of the periphery of the optic nerve... had indirectly provoked a subjective and durable sensation

attributions.surface_quote: my reminiscence, incorporating itself with this subjective sensation, became the corpse-like phantom

attributions.surface_quote: We must choose fitting points or lines in the background with which to compare the positions of its head

canonical_statement: The perceived character of an object can be altered by changing the frame of reference or observational conditions.

attributions.chapter: part vi. chaps. ix, x. E. v. Hartmann, Phil. of the Unconscious (B),
attributions.surface_quote: what a singular hopping and rocking appearance he presents!

canonical_statement: Certain qualities of an object are more readily perceived than others, depending on observational conditions.

attributions.chapter: part vi. chaps. ix, x. E. v. Hartmann, Phil. of the Unconscious (B),
attributions.surface_quote: its total character... is harder to perceive than in the upright position.

attributions.surface_quote: internal images... become intense, distinct, colored, steady, and lasting

attributions.surface_quote: the intense image which seems an external object is but a more forcible continuation

attributions.surface_quote: persistence of dream-objects for a few moments after the eyes are opened

canonical_statement: Sensory modalities possess varying degrees of perceived spatial extent or 'voluminousness'.

attributions.surface_quote: In the sensations of hearing, touch, sight, and pain we are accustomed to distinguish... the element of voluminousness.

canonical_statement: The perception of spatiality is a component of subjective motion sensations.

attributions.surface_quote: In the sensation of dizziness or subjective motion... the spatial character is very prominent.

canonical_statement: The muscular sense may contribute to the cognition of spatial extension.

attributions.surface_quote: Whether the 'muscular sense' directly yields us knowledge of space is still a matter of litigation.

canonical_statement: Some tastes and smells are perceived as having less spatial extent than others.

attributions.surface_quote: In the sensations of smell and taste this element of varying vastness seems less prominent but not altogether absent.

canonical_statement: Spatial awareness is an intrinsic element of all sensations, not merely a property of external objects.

attributions.surface_quote: this element, discernible in each and every sensation, though more developed in some than in others, is the original sensation of space

canonical_statement: The capacity to perceive and subdivide spatial extensity varies across different sensory organs.

attributions.surface_quote: The ear gives a greater vastness than the skin, but is considerably less able to subdivide it.

canonical_statement: The consciousness of bodily states possesses a spatial quality.

attributions.surface_quote: Our entire cubic content seems then sensibly manifest to us as such

canonical_statement: The retina provides the most extensive spatial perception and the greatest capacity for subdividing it.

attributions.surface_quote: the maximal vastness yielded by the retina surpass that yielded by any other organ

canonical_statement: The perceived spatial extent of phenomena is comparable across different sensory modalities.

attributions.surface_quote: Sensations of different orders are roughly comparable, inter se, with respect to their volumes.

canonical_statement: Spatial quality is a fundamental and shared characteristic of sensory experience.

attributions.surface_quote: This shows that the spatial quality in each is identical wherever found

canonical_statement: Certain phenomena, such as intense sounds or luminous objects, possess an inherent quality of spatial vastness.

attributions.surface_quote: Loud sounds have a certain enormousness of feeling. A glowing iron looks luminous through and through

canonical_statement: Sensations can possess spatial volume, extending beyond mere surface perception.

attributions.surface_quote: a space filled with darkness, and even when we succeed in seeing this darkness as terminated by a black wall there still remains in front of this wall the dark space.

attributions.surface_quote: By day the so-called empty space between us and objects seen appears very different from what it is by night.

canonical_statement: Internal shifts in attention can be accompanied by proprioceptive sensations suggesting spatial movement within the body.

attributions.surface_quote: quasi-motor sensations in the head when we change the direction of the attention

attributions.surface_quote: When we transfer the attention from objects of one sense to those of another we have... a feeling of altered direction, or differently localized tension.

attributions.surface_quote: the feeling withdraws entirely from the external sense-organs, and seems rather to take refuge in that part of the head which the brain fills.

attributions.surface_quote: the feeling itself, however, is not projected fully into the spot

attributions.surface_quote: the experiment shows that the same object gives more of it to the inner than to the outer cuticle

attributions.surface_quote: primitive perceptions of space are certainly of an unordered kind.

attributions.surface_quote: order must be woven into those spaces by a rather complicated set of intellectual acts.

attributions.surface_quote: form by their synthesis what we know as the real Space of the objective world.

attributions.surface_quote: they nowhere add any new material to the space-data of sense

attributions.surface_quote: sense-spaces...should tend...to enter into any definite spatial intercourse

attributions.surface_quote: feelings may coexist in us without assuming any particular spatial order

canonical_statement: The perception of the body's spatial order is often vague and ambiguous unless attention is uniformly distributed.

attributions.surface_quote: vague and ambiguous our perception of their relative order of location is

attributions.surface_quote: feel the real shape of our body in a sort of unitary way

attributions.surface_quote: sensible extents ... in definite order they must appear as parts in a vaster sensible extent

attributions.surface_quote: objective spaces too great to be grasped by a single look ... have to be thus constructed from data apprehended in succession

attributions.surface_quote: That a sensation be discriminated as a part from out of a larger enveloping space is then the conditio sine quâ non of its being apprehended in a definite spatial order.

attributions.surface_quote: discrimination, but not of discrimination pure and simple; for then not only coexistent sights but coexistent sounds would necessarily assume such order

attributions.surface_quote: Spatial order is an abstract term. The concrete perceptions which it covers are figures, directions, positions, magnitudes, and distances.

canonical_statement: Introducing order into a vastness involves singling out discrete elements from it.

attributions.surface_quote: To single out any one of these things from a total vastness is partially to introduce order into the vastness.

canonical_statement: The apprehension of a vastness as completely orderly is achieved by subdividing it into discrete elements.

attributions.surface_quote: To subdivide the vastness into a multitude of these things is to apprehend it in a completely orderly way.

canonical_statement: Figures, such as shapes and lines, are perceived as distinct qualities of sensation.

attributions.surface_quote: no one can for an instant hesitate to say that some of them are qualities of sensation, just as the total vastness is in which they lie.

canonical_statement: The perception of spatial relations, such as distance and direction, is distinct from the perception of sensory qualities.

canonical_statement: Relations are considered energies of pure thought, separate from sensory data.

attributions.surface_quote: And not one of these determinations can be effected except through an act of relating thought.

canonical_statement: Thought is the ultimate faculty for understanding the nature of space.

attributions.surface_quote: Thought alone can unlock the riddle of space, and that Thought is an adorable but unfathomable mystery.

attributions.surface_quote: in the field of space the relations are facts of the same order with the facts they relate.

attributions.surface_quote: nor can you in any conceivable way think the latter except by imagining the former

attributions.surface_quote: Rightness and leftness, upness and downness, are again pure sensations

attributions.surface_quote: Like all sensations, they can only be indicated, not described.

attributions.surface_quote: the relation of quantity is generic and occurs in many categories of consciousness

attributions.surface_quote: all space-relations except those of magnitude are nothing more or less than pure sensational objects

attributions.surface_quote: This transitional sensation of 'more' must be identical with itself under all these different accompaniments

attributions.surface_quote: the mind must get the immediate feeling of an outstanding 'plus'

attributions.surface_quote: all spatial knowledge is sensational at bottom

attributions.surface_quote: They are nothing but sensations of particular lines, particular angles, particular forms of transition

canonical_statement: Spatial qualities are immanent to sensations, not externally imposed.

attributions.surface_quote: sensations are from the outset localized...affected with the spatial quality

attributions.surface_quote: stomach-feeling seems to lie somewhere in this vastness

attributions.surface_quote: there are two ways of combining sight and touch perceptions.

attributions.surface_quote: throughout all this confusion we conceive of a world spread out in a perfectly fixed and orderly fashion

attributions.surface_quote: we invoke the articular cartilages, as internal surfaces whose sensibility is called in play

attributions.surface_quote: assume the articular surfaces to be the seat of the perception in question

attributions.surface_quote: the joint-surfaces are sensitive

attributions.surface_quote: either of which exclusively it may notice, or both at once

attributions.surface_quote: implies the pre-existence of certain nerves arranged in a certain way.

attributions.surface_quote: established relations among its parts stand for so many established relations among the psychical changes.

canonical_statement: The human brain functions as a repository for the accumulated experiences of ancestral organisms throughout evolutionary history.

attributions.surface_quote: the human brain is an organized register of infinitely-numerous experiences received during the evolution of life

attributions.surface_quote: The effects of the most uniform and frequent of these experiences have been successively bequeathed... and have slowly amounted to that high intelligence which lies latent in the brain of the infant

canonical_statement: Mental content derived from internal biological processes does not necessarily reflect the nature of those processes.

attributions.chapter: TWO MODES OF ORIGIN OF BRAIN STRUCTURE.

attributions.chapter: TWO MODES OF ORIGIN OF BRAIN STRUCTURE.

attributions.chapter: TWO MODES OF ORIGIN OF BRAIN STRUCTURE.

attributions.chapter: TWO MODES OF ORIGIN OF BRAIN STRUCTURE.

canonical_statement: Consciousness is composed of elementary sensory and affective components.

attributions.surface_quote: Emotions; desires; instincts; ideas of worth; æsthetic ideas

canonical_statement: Fundamental concepts of time, space, and number are inherent to consciousness.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE ELEMENTARY MENTAL CATEGORIES.
attributions.surface_quote: Ideas of time and space and number

canonical_statement: Consciousness apprehends relations of difference, resemblance, and their gradations.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE ELEMENTARY MENTAL CATEGORIES.
attributions.surface_quote: Ideas of difference and resemblance, and of their degrees

canonical_statement: Consciousness perceives causal relationships, purpose, and inherent properties.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE ELEMENTARY MENTAL CATEGORIES.
attributions.surface_quote: Ideas of causal dependence among events; of end and means

attributions.surface_quote: mind gifted with memory, expectation, and the possibility of feeling doubt, curiosity, belief, and denial

canonical_statement: The perception of objective differences is either a product of innate mental structures or an accurate apprehension of external reality.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: subjective reason can only be that our minds were so constructed

canonical_statement: The frequency of past experiences can shape the necessity of present cognitive forms.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: because they simply did differ so often that at last they begat

attributions.surface_quote: explanation of our difference-judgment is absolutely unintelligible

attributions.surface_quote: mind must needs know it--which is no explanation at all

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: consciousness could feel the transition from one term to another

canonical_statement: The perception of difference and resemblance is an inherent activity of the mind.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: the mind feels its own activity

canonical_statement: The determination of difference and resemblance between concepts is independent of empirical existence.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: the mere ideas suffice

canonical_statement: Propositions derived from comparing concepts are classified as rational propositions.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: rational propositions to all propositions which express the results of a comparison

canonical_statement: Propositions concerning time and space relations are classified as empirical propositions.

attributions.chapter: THE GENESIS OF THE PURE SCIENCES.
attributions.surface_quote: call all propositions which express time- and space-relations empirical propositions

canonical_statement: The comparison of identical objects under identical conditions yields a constant and immutable result.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: The same objects, compared in the same way, always give the same results

canonical_statement: The fundamental principle of mental operations is that identical inputs processed by identical methods produce identical outputs.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: the Same operated on in the same way gives the Same

canonical_statement: Mental objects and their perceived differences constitute a fixed and unchanging system.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: The objects and their differences together form an immutable system

canonical_statement: Consciousness can perform meta-analysis on its own comparative operations, generating higher-order comparisons.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: the operation of comparing may be repeated on its own results

canonical_statement: Consciousness apprehends serial progressions characterized by a constant directional increment.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: forms series of terms with the same kind and amount of difference

canonical_statement: The magnitude of difference between two entities is proportional to their serial distance.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: two terms taken far apart differ more than two terms taken near together

canonical_statement: The structure of comparative relationships remains invariant regardless of the specific entities or nature of the comparison, provided the comparative operation is consistent.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: no matter what the terms may be, or what the sort of difference

canonical_statement: Abstract relational structures can be represented and manipulated symbolically, with intermediate elements being omissible without altering the fundamental relationship.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: any number of intermediaries may be expunged without obliging us to alter anything

canonical_statement: Relations between terms remain invariant when intermediary terms are omitted.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: skipping intermediary terms leaves relations the same

canonical_statement: The principle of invariant relations through omitted intermediaries is a fundamental law of thought.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: broadest and deepest law of man's thought

canonical_statement: Equality between terms remains invariant when intermediary terms are omitted.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: axiom of mediate equality, 'equals of equals are equal'

canonical_statement: Mathematical principles of equality are derived from the mind's inherent acuity, independent of experiential order.

attributions.chapter: SERIES OF EVEN DIFFERENCE AND MEDIATE COMPARISON.
attributions.surface_quote: mind's mere acuteness, and in utter independence of the order

canonical_statement: Ideal truths of comparison exist, forming an immutable system applicable to all terms of experience, regardless of order or frequency.

attributions.surface_quote: ideal truths of comparison, a system applicable to terms experienced in any order of sequence or frequency

canonical_statement: The mind derives aesthetic satisfaction from classifying experienced materials into serial orders.

attributions.surface_quote: a great æsthetic delight for the mind to break the order of experience, and class its materials

canonical_statement: A world whose materials naturally lend themselves to serial classification is perceived as more rational and intimate.

attributions.surface_quote: a world whose real materials naturally lend themselves to serial classification is pro tanto a more rational world

canonical_statement: The ability to serially classify facts is a manifestation of divine thought within nature.

attributions.surface_quote: classifications were supposed to be ultimate insights into God's mind, filling us with adoration of his ways

canonical_statement: The failure of experience to conform to serial classification indicates a lack of rationality.

attributions.surface_quote: so far as the facts of experience can not be serially classified, therefore, so far experience fails to be rational

canonical_statement: The faculty of apprehending serial increase makes consciousness aware of successive terms united by a relation as a single system.

attributions.surface_quote: conscious of them as a single system of successive terms united by the same relation

canonical_statement: The principle of mediate predication states that any earlier term in a series of predications stands in the same relation to any later term as it does to any intermediate term.

attributions.surface_quote: The principle of mediate predication or subsumption

canonical_statement: Whatever possesses an attribute also possesses all the attributes of that attribute.

attributions.surface_quote: whatever has an attribute has all the attributes of that attribute

canonical_statement: Whatever belongs to a kind also belongs to the kind's kind.

attributions.surface_quote: whatever is of a kind is of that kind's kind

canonical_statement: Consciousness selects aspects of reality based on practical purpose, substituting these aspects for the whole.

attributions.surface_quote: we substitute the aspect for the whole real thing.

canonical_statement: The linguistic copula 'is' signifies an act of identification between a whole and its aspect or attribute.

attributions.surface_quote: the word _is_ ... expresses ... the identifying operation performed.

canonical_statement: The logical structure of predication can functionally mirror mathematical equations for practical purposes.

attributions.surface_quote: The predication-series _a_ is _b... resembles ... the equation-series _a = b...

canonical_statement: The purpose of predication is to satisfy curiosity about an object's classification relative to a goal.

attributions.surface_quote: our purpose in predicating? ... it is always the gratification of a certain curiosity

canonical_statement: Attributes or aspects of an object can be treated as equivalent to the object itself, provided the specific purpose is maintained.

attributions.surface_quote: Sirius's attribute is, Sirius is; its adjective's adjective can supersede its own adjective

canonical_statement: The meaning of 'is' allows for the elimination of intermediary terms in a series, treating remote terms as equivalent to proximate ones.

attributions.surface_quote: elimination of intermediary kinds and transfer of _is_'s along the line, results from our insight into the very meaning of the word _is_

canonical_statement: The principle of mediate subsumption, which allows dropping intermediaries in a series, is based on the meaning of relations, not on the specific order or co-existence of experiences.

attributions.surface_quote: the principle of mediate subsumption has nothing to do with the particular order of our experiences

canonical_statement: When a perceived object does not conform to the properties of its designated kind, the error lies in the designation or the understanding of the properties, not in the principle of classification itself.

attributions.surface_quote: if the thing we named an M has not M's properties, then we were either mistaken in calling it an M

canonical_statement: The conceptualization of a thing as belonging to a kind implies that it inherently possesses the properties of that kind, regardless of empirical verification.

attributions.surface_quote: by conceiving a thing as of the kind M I mean that it _shall_ have M's properties

canonical_statement: The perception of the meaning of successive 'is' relations is independent of and cannot be altered by external empirical facts.

attributions.surface_quote: This perception can no more be confirmed by one set, or weakened by another set, of outer facts

canonical_statement: Formal logic describes the relations between terms connected by identity, and their possibilities of substitution.

attributions.surface_quote: Formal logic is the name of the Science which traces... relations of terms connected by successive is's

canonical_statement: The principle of substitution states that identical entities can be substituted for each other in any mental operation.

attributions.surface_quote: the same can be substituted for the same in any mental operation.

canonical_statement: The capacity to apprehend a series of more than two terms simultaneously is the basis of reasoning.

attributions.surface_quote: The ground of there being any logic at all is our power to grasp any series as a whole

canonical_statement: Logic and systematic classification are emergent properties of the capacity to discern difference and likeness.

attributions.surface_quote: both Systematic Classification and Logic are seen to be incidental results of the mere capacity for discerning difference and likeness

canonical_statement: The order of experience is independent of the fundamental capacity for discerning difference and likeness.

attributions.surface_quote: which capacity is a thing with which the order of experience... has absolutely nothing to do.

canonical_statement: The logical relations among phenomena possess significant utility for understanding the facts of existence.

attributions.surface_quote: logical relations among things should form such a mighty engine for dealing with the facts of life

canonical_statement: Reality possesses inherent kinds and enduring properties that allow for logical inference and practical application.

attributions.chapter: Chapter XXII already gave the reason (see p. 335, above). This world
attributions.surface_quote: our world is no such world. It is a very peculiar world, and plays right into logic's hands.

canonical_statement: The apprehension of serial increase and remote connections between entities is a fundamental intellectual operation.

attributions.chapter: Chapter XXII already gave the reason (see p. 335, above). This world
attributions.surface_quote: The flight to this last kind over the heads of the intermediaries is the essential feature of the intellectual operation here.

canonical_statement: The logical structure of reality is independent of the temporal and spatial experience of its constituents.

attributions.chapter: Chapter XXII already gave the reason (see p. 335, above). This world
attributions.surface_quote: it has nothing to do with the time- and space-order in which the things have been experienced.

canonical_statement: Mathematical judgments are rational propositions that express results of comparison.

attributions.surface_quote: mathematical judgments... express results of comparison and nothing more.

canonical_statement: Mathematical sciences exclusively deal with similarities and equalities, not coexistences and sequences.

attributions.surface_quote: The mathematical sciences deal with similarities and equalities exclusively, and not with coexistences and sequences.

canonical_statement: Mathematical comparisons are between numbers and extensive magnitudes, giving rise to arithmetic and geometry.

attributions.surface_quote: The comparisons of mathematics are between numbers and extensive magnitudes, giving rise to arithmetic and geometry respectively.

canonical_statement: The perception of number arises from the mind's act of discriminating and grouping discrete phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: Number seems to signify primarily the strokes of our attention in discriminating things.

canonical_statement: The quantity attributed to a phenomenon is contingent upon the observer's method of segmentation and counting.

attributions.surface_quote: the number of things which any one given phenomenon may be depends in the last instance on our way of taking it.

canonical_statement: Mathematical series possess inherent relational properties that are recognized independently of the specific terms within the series.

attributions.surface_quote: like all lists of terms in which there is a direction of serial increase, carries with it the sense of those mediate relations between its terms

canonical_statement: The fundamental units of numerical quantity remain invariant despite operations of grouping or interruption.

attributions.surface_quote: The matter is the original units or strokes; which all modes of grouping or combining simply give us back unchanged.

canonical_statement: Combinations of numbers are fundamentally equivalent to combinations of their constituent units.

attributions.surface_quote: combinations of numbers are combinations of their units

canonical_statement: The consistency of numerical results is guaranteed by the unchanging nature of the underlying units and the operations performed.

attributions.surface_quote: the same number, operated on (interrupted, grouped) in the same way will always give the same result or be the same.

canonical_statement: The fundamental principles of arithmetic are independent of empirical experience and the structure of the external world.

attributions.surface_quote: Arithmetic and its fundamental principles are thus independent of our experiences or of the order of the world.

canonical_statement: Mathematical truths are derived from the inherent nature of mental constructs, not from observations of external phenomena.

attributions.surface_quote: The matter of arithmetic is mental matter; its principles flow from the fact that the matter forms a series

canonical_statement: The empiricist view that numerical truths are derived from sensory experiences of external objects is incorrect.

attributions.surface_quote: The empiricist school has strangely tried to interpret the truths of number as results of coexistences among outward things.

canonical_statement: The equivalence of mathematical expressions is not solely based on the accumulation of empirical evidence.

attributions.surface_quote: The indefeasibility of our belief in their 'coexistence' ... is due solely to the enormous amount of experience we have of it.

canonical_statement: Mathematical truths derive their certainty from abstract, ideal concepts, not from physical experience.

attributions.surface_quote: Our arithmetical propositions would never have the confident tone which they now possess.

canonical_statement: The meaning of mathematical operations is determined by human intention, independent of physical outcomes.

attributions.surface_quote: What we mean by one plus one is two; we make two out of it.

canonical_statement: Abstract numbers are ideal objects that remain constant, unlike concrete natural things which can be counted in multiple ways.

attributions.surface_quote: Only the abstract numbers themselves are unequivocal, only those which we create mentally.

canonical_statement: The numerical properties of experienced phenomena are not inherently stable but are subject to change.

attributions.surface_quote: Sensibly, however, things are constantly changing their numbers

canonical_statement: The application of arithmetic to reality requires the imposition of numerical continuity not spontaneously found in experience.

attributions.surface_quote: we must somehow make more numerical continuity than we spontaneously find

canonical_statement: Scientific models can abstract stable numerical properties from phenomena, even when sensible experience does not present them.

attributions.surface_quote: hypothetic atoms... will stay numbered all the time

canonical_statement: The perceived world is not the ultimate reality for science; rather, it is a construct based on stable, quantifiable elements.

attributions.surface_quote: Sensible things are not the things for me, says Science

canonical_statement: Mathematical forms are ideal creations independent of their instantiation in nature.

attributions.surface_quote: Its objects are also ideal creations.

canonical_statement: The logical and mathematical principles governing abstract forms are universally applicable to conceptual objects.

attributions.surface_quote: The axioms of mediate comparison, of logic, and of number all apply to the forms which we imagine in space.

canonical_statement: Geometric forms like straight lines and planes are conceptual constructs derived from the mind's capacity for serial progression, not direct perceptions of external reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Straight lines, planes, and parallels, as they figure in geometry, are mere inventions of our faculty for apprehending serial increase.

canonical_statement: The perceived uniformity and beauty of geometric forms stem from the assumption of consistent direction and adherence to a defined concept.

attributions.surface_quote: This uniformity of direction throughout is, in fact, all that makes us care for these forms, gives them their beauty, and stamps them into fixed conceptions in our mind.

canonical_statement: Deviations from geometric ideals like straightness or planarity are equivalent to changes in direction or relation to pre-existing parts.

attributions.surface_quote: Parting company in lines and planes _means_ changing direction, means assuming a new relation to the parts that pre-exist; and assuming a new relation means ceasing to be straight or plane.

canonical_statement: The concept of parallel lines is maintained by the principle of consistent direction, where any deviation implies a failure to remain parallel.

attributions.surface_quote: No properties of outlying space need come in here: only a definite conception of uniform direction, and constancy in sticking to one's point.

canonical_statement: The spatial arrangement of a whole is irrelevant to its total quantity.

attributions.surface_quote: no variation in the way of subdividing a given amount of space alters its total quantity

canonical_statement: The identity of a form is invariant under translation through space.

attributions.surface_quote: fixed equalities and differences obtain between forms, no matter where placed

canonical_statement: The fundamental relations between forms are independent of their specific instantiation in experienced reality.

attributions.surface_quote: regardless of whether the figures we speak of have ever been outwardly experienced or not

canonical_statement: The capacity to perceive and distinguish series is a fundamental aspect of consciousness that enables rational thought.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: consciousness of series is the basis of rationality

canonical_statement: The laws governing thought are not purely formal but are derived from the nature of the objects being thought about.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: it flows from the nature of the matters thought about

canonical_statement: The ability to apprehend series is an evolved human perfection, not solely a result of external associations.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: consciousness of series is a human perfection which has been gradually evolved

canonical_statement: The axiom of skipped intermediaries applies only to specific types of series, not universally.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: axiom of skipped intermediaries applies, however, only to certain particular series

canonical_statement: The transferability of relations within a series is an intrinsic property of the series, not merely a linguistic convention.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: relations which are intrinsically transferable, whilst others are not

canonical_statement: The relation of conditionality is intrinsically transferable across intermediaries.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: The relation of condition, e.g., is intrinsically transferable.

canonical_statement: The relations of negation and frustration are not intrinsically transferable across intermediaries.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: relations of negation and frustration... are not transferable

canonical_statement: The inherent nature of ideas determines their possible connections and relations.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Their connections, immediate and remote, flow from their inward natures.

canonical_statement: The possibility of deriving new perceptions from the combination of conceived objects reflects their essential connections.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: whether there are or are not inward and essential connections between conceived objects as such, really is the same thing as the question whether we can get any new perception from mentally coupling them together

canonical_statement: The mind apprehends necessary and eternal relations between ideal conceptions, forming a system independent of empirical experience.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: the mind is filled with necessary and eternal relations which it finds between certain of its ideal conceptions, and which form a determinate system, independent of the order of frequency in which experience may have associated the conception's originals in time and space.

canonical_statement: General knowledge is derived from the contemplation of abstract ideas within the mind.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: All general knowledge lies only in our own thoughts, and consists barely in the contemplation of our abstract ideas.

canonical_statement: Truths concerning the essences of things are eternal and discoverable through contemplation of those essences.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Truths belonging to essences of things (that is, to abstract ideas) are eternal, and are to be found out only by the contemplation of those essences.

canonical_statement: Eternal truths are propositions about abstract ideas that remain true regardless of when they are considered.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Such propositions are therefore called 'eternal truths,'... because, being once made about abstract ideas so as to be true, they will, whenever they can be supposed to be made again, at any time past or to come, by a mind having those ideas, always actually be true.

canonical_statement: The immutability of relations between immutable things grounds certainty in general truths.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: The immutability of the same relations between the same immutable things is now the idea that shows him that if the three angles of a triangle were once equal to two right angles, they will always be equal to two right ones.

canonical_statement: Knowledge is the consequence of the relationships between ideas present in the mind.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Knowledge is the consequence of the ideas (be they what they will) that are in our minds, producing there certain general propositions.

canonical_statement: The fundamental nature of consciousness is the recognition of relations of likeness and difference between elements within a series.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: relations of likeness and difference, immediate or mediate, between the terms of certain series

canonical_statement: Rational operations such as classification, logic, arithmetic, and geometry are forms of serial comparison and relation-finding.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Classification is serial comparison, logic mediate subsumption, arithmetic mediate equality

canonical_statement: Abstract verities discovered by consciousness (e.g., logic, mathematics, geometry) are independent of empirical facts and do not assert the existence or reality of external phenomena.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: None of these eternal verities has anything to say about facts, about what is or is not in the world

canonical_statement: The validity of abstract verities is conditional upon the hypothetical existence of the phenomena they describe.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: if these things are anywhere to be found, the eternal verities will obtain of them

canonical_statement: Knowledge of abstract ideas is certain and independent of empirical existence.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: universal propositions of whose truth or falsehood we can have certain knowledge, concern not existence

canonical_statement: The certainty of knowledge regarding abstract ideas relies solely on the internal coherence and distinctness of those ideas.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: their certainty is founded only upon the knowledge of each idea by itself

canonical_statement: Mathematical truths derived from abstract ideas hold true for real-world objects only to the extent that those objects conform to the abstract ideas.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: real things are no farther concerned nor intended to be meant by any such propositions, than as things really agree to those archetypes in his mind

canonical_statement: Knowledge of the existence of material objects is contingent upon sensory experience, not abstract reasoning.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: that any or what bodies do exist, that we are left to our senses to discover

canonical_statement: The truth of propositions about abstract concepts is distinct from the truth of propositions about empirical reality.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Locke accordingly distinguishes between 'mental truth' and 'real truth.'

canonical_statement: Affirming the applicability of abstract truths to reality is a hypothetical act based on assumed correspondence.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Only hypothetically can we affirm intuitive truths of real things--by supposing ... that real things exist which correspond exactly with the ideal subjects

canonical_statement: A priori propositions were historically considered to reveal the fundamental structure of reality.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: By the ancients they were considered to reveal the constitution of Reality.

canonical_statement: The mind's inherent logical necessities were once believed to correspond to the necessities of existence.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: The mind's necessities were a warrant for those of Being

canonical_statement: Intuitive propositions or mental structures do not necessarily correspond to or guarantee extra-mental reality.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: the eternal verities... do not necessarily themselves lay hold on extra-mental being

canonical_statement: The validity of intuitive propositions is primarily a subjective phenomenon.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: They are primarily interesting only as subjective facts.

canonical_statement: The fundamental reality of the universe consists of unperceived, mathematically describable entities in motion.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Atoms and ether, with no properties but masses and velocities expressible by numbers

canonical_statement: Sensible phenomena and perceived qualities are illusory and do not constitute true reality.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Sensible phenomena are pure delusions for the mechanical philosophy.

canonical_statement: The universe's history is determined by the motion and arrangement of fundamental entities, deducible from initial conditions.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: swarming solids in everlasting motion... deducible from initial collocations

canonical_statement: Systems of understanding based on teleology, aesthetics, or sentiment are less effective for describing reality than mathematical systems.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: The most promising of these ideal systems at first were of course the richer ones, the sentimental ones.

canonical_statement: Attributing sentimental, moral, or aesthetic qualities to natural phenomena does not alter their natural consequences or inherent properties.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: Call the things of nature as much as you like by sentimental... names, no natural consequences follow

canonical_statement: The universe is fundamentally composed of primordial matter in motion, governed by deterministic laws.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: collocations and motions of primordial solids, and the only laws the changes of motion

canonical_statement: A complete understanding of reality can be achieved through a mathematical formula that predicts all future states from initial conditions.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: mathematical world-formula, by which, if all the collocations and motions at a given moment were known

canonical_statement: The perceived qualities and affections of the world are illusory, lacking inherent substance.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: things and qualities men love... are but illusions of our fancy

canonical_statement: The human drive to find rational connections between phenomena is the origin of scientific inquiry.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: craving to believe that the things of the world belong to kinds which are related by inward rationality

canonical_statement: The aim of theoretical physics is to discover the ultimate, unchanging causes of natural processes.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: The ultimate goal of theoretic physics is to find the last unchanging causes of the processes in Nature.

canonical_statement: The scientific method presupposes the intelligibility of nature, proceeding with this assumption until contradictory evidence arises.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: the Science whose aim it is to make nature appear intelligible must start with the assumption of her intelligibility

canonical_statement: Natural phenomena are ultimately reducible to motions of material points governed by invariant motor forces dependent solely on spatial relations.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: The phenomena of nature must be reduced to motions of material points with inalterable motor forces

canonical_statement: The fundamental forces in nature are invariant over time and their intensity is solely a function of distance.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: forces unchanged by time must be found to be these causes... its intensity can only depend on distance.

canonical_statement: The rational order of the experienced world is a consequence of its conceptualization as composed of fundamental units possessing only quantifiable properties like number and motion.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: the world grows more orderly and rational to the mind

canonical_statement: Scientific theories are validated when the experienced world behaves in accordance with abstract, idealized models.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: the things of Nature turn out to act as if they were of the kind assumed

canonical_statement: The predictability of phenomena through mathematical and mechanical models justifies their conceptual primacy over direct sensory experience.

attributions.chapter: CONSCIOUSNESS OF SERIES IS THE BASIS OF RATIONALITY.
attributions.surface_quote: declarations which are justified by the appearance of new sensible experiences

canonical_statement: The fundamental principle of reality is singular.

attributions.surface_quote: The Principle of things is one

canonical_statement: The total amount of existence remains constant.

attributions.surface_quote: The quantity of existence is unchanged

canonical_statement: Natural processes are characterized by simplicity and immutability.

attributions.surface_quote: Nature is simple and invariable

canonical_statement: Nature operates through the most efficient or direct means.

attributions.surface_quote: Nature acts by the shortest ways

canonical_statement: Nothing arises from absolute nothingness.

attributions.surface_quote: Ex nihilo nihil fit

canonical_statement: All that is manifested was implicitly present in its origin.

attributions.surface_quote: Nothing can be evolved which was not involved

canonical_statement: The effect is contained within the cause.

attributions.surface_quote: Whatever is in the effect must be in the cause

canonical_statement: Entities can only exert influence within their immediate vicinity.

attributions.surface_quote: A thing can only work where it is

canonical_statement: Entities can only affect others of their own kind.

attributions.surface_quote: A thing can only affect another of its own kind

canonical_statement: The cessation of a cause leads to the cessation of its effect.

attributions.surface_quote: Cessante causa, cessat et effectus

canonical_statement: Natural progression is continuous, without abrupt jumps.

attributions.surface_quote: Nature makes no leaps

canonical_statement: Entities belong to distinct and enduring categories.

attributions.surface_quote: Things belong to discrete and permanent kinds

canonical_statement: All phenomena have a determining reason or cause.

attributions.surface_quote: Nothing is or happens without a reason

canonical_statement: The universe is fundamentally comprehensible through reason.

attributions.surface_quote: The world is throughout rationally intelligible

canonical_statement: The conservation of energy is a principle observed in nature.

attributions.surface_quote: the 'quantity of existence' so vaguely postulated as unchanged, Nature allows us to suppose that curious sum of distances and velocities which for want of a better term we call 'energy.'

canonical_statement: The effect is identical to the cause when viewed at a fundamental level.

attributions.surface_quote: the effect _is_ the cause,' so soon as she lets us conceive both effect and cause as the same molecules, in two successive positions
